items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: There is a marvelous story about this. Bunny Berigan was playing with Tommy Dorsey...

ctx.x: Well, if he were cruel, excuse me. I doubt very much that he is aware of it, because I have known him to do some very kind things. But I knew Tommy Dorsey to be -- really do some lovely things for people

and he was a hard, cruel man at times.
On the bandstand, get him off the bandstand, again he was very -- if he loved a band's playing, he would do anything for them. There is a marvelous story about this. Bunny Berigan was playing with Tommy Dorsey and one night he got terribly drunk and they were playing at the Pennsylvania Hotel and there is his music, strewn all over the bandstand, his stand is over, and he is lying there completely passed out.

Tommy's manager came up to Tommy and said, 'Why don't you fire that son of a bitch' and Tommy said, 'I can't fire him, he plays too good.' So you see, he had this wonderful -- he had wonderful respect for people who could play. Jazz soloists. Tommy is not a jazz man himself, but he did play some pretty nice things. He was a magnificent trombone player.
